chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Hearing the Bix records and race
summary: Joe says they were told the Bix and Trumbauer records were by White musicians, and the new style took Black and White musicians by storm.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: I don't want to get into any particular racial things here. But you were talking about the Bix Beiderbecke record. When you first heard that, did you know they were White guys playing?
Were you told they were, or could you tell?
We was wondering who it was... Because they had come up with such a distinct style! And today, though, those are nice records. Good arrangements, well-played to my idea. I just like them.
Could you have told that they were White musicians by listening to the records?

Well, in a way. We figured it wasn't any Black musicians or Colored musicians played that style, and naturally it was talked, it's a new White band there in Chicago or wherever they was playing. And it took the whole music business by storm, White and Black musicians. That... When I first heard Louis play and these records really... It left a heck of an impression on me.
